accuracy.evidence: Checked against the Common Core State Standards for Mathematics grade 1 measurement standard 1.MD.1 (order three objects by length; compare the lengths of two objects indirectly by using a third object), quoted in the adult text, and the Illustrative Mathematics grade 1 unit on length (indirect comparison with string, lining up endpoints). Transitivity is stated as a rule about lengths only; ribbon lengths 9, 7 and 5 units and the 8-unit gap against the 7-unit sofa are drawn to scale with one shared unit, so every on-screen comparison is true.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the slips reported in Clements and Sarama's learning trajectory for length (Learning and Teaching Early Math, ch. 10) and the Nunes and Bryant work on transitive reasoning: judging length by the end that reaches furthest without aligning starts (prediction 1, 'far' feedback, p1), a sagging or curled string (prediction 3, 'wavy', p5), a go-between shorter than both objects (prediction 5, 'stick', m3), reversing the order of a transitive chain ('flip', m1) and believing indirect comparison is impossible ('cant', p3).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagindir is built around indirect comparison: ragged ribbons that must be moved to a start line in order, a string knot dragged across a gap and carried to a sofa that cannot move, a wavy string whose laid-flat length visibly exceeds the gap until it is pulled tight, three children behind doors compared two at a time, and a short stick that cannot decide against a string that can. flaglenht only lines up two bars and counts cubes. Gate lab_distinct passes (every other flagship lab under 30% 6-shingle overlap).

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner discovers each idea before the text names it: the blue ribbon that reaches furthest lands in the 'shortest' slot once moved to the start line; the sofa result only appears after the string is stretched to the wall and carried; the laid-flat copy of the wavy string shrinks to the dashed gap outline as the learner pulls; Ali and Cat are never compared directly, yet the final line-up confirms Ali is tallest; the stick leaves the question open while the string settles it.

predictions.evidence: Four predictions, each with a tempting wrong option the lab then disproves: 'Blue: it reaches furthest' (blue is shortest once lined up), 'No, never' for comparing things that cannot meet (the string does it), 'just right' for a wavy string (its flat copy is too long), and 'We cannot know' for Ali against Cat (the chain decides, then the reveal confirms). Step 5 adds 'Yes' for the short stick, disproved when both objects beat it.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Seven challenge questions with nine distinct feedback messages naming the slip: reaching furthest is not longest; flipping the chain; 'you can tell' when a child thinks indirect comparison is impossible; guessing by eye; wavy string measures too long; a stick shorter than both cannot decide; 4 is shorter than 6 so it goes in the middle; Sam is not shortest. Each wrong answer is followed by a fresh question.

readability.evidence: Kid explanation reads at FK grade 1.4 with short sentences and the target words longer, shorter, longest, start, string, go-between; adult text averages well under the 9.5 limit and lists key vocabulary and the 1.MD.1 wording. Lab step text is two or three short sentences; the challenge uses names and small numbers (2, 4, 6 blocks) suited to ages 6-7, and the lab uses the young layout with 56 px buttons.

no_filler.evidence: Gate finds no filler phrases. Each kid paragraph teaches one move (line up starts; carry a length with string; keep it tight; the transitive chain). Items each test a distinct move: p2 and m6 compute how much longer the string is, p4 picks the longest of three, m5 reasons from a string matched to the door, m9 says why the eye is not enough. Hints point to the reasoning, not the answer.

mobile.evidence: Checked on iPhone 13 screenshots in light and dark: ribbons, slots and labels fit the 390 px canvas with the tall layout; the string knot has a 16 px radius and the pull handle sits at the right edge as a large target; the doors and children use a third of the width each; controls wrap to two or three rows of 56 px young buttons and nothing is clipped. Dark theme start line, slots and string were recoloured after the first screenshots showed low contrast.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a labelled button: a button per ribbon plus Try again, Stretch to the wall and Take string to sofa, Pull tighter and Make it wavy, Ali and Ben, Ben and Cat and a tallest button per child, Use a short stick and Use a string. The canvas aria-label is updated with each result, the challenge feedback is a polite live region, and walk.cjs axe WCAG 2.1 AA is clean in both themes on desktop and iPhone 13.
